candidates.source_name: Petrol d.d. – Aktualno / obvestila za medije (press room)
candidates.why_relevant: Petrol is Slovenia's largest fuel/convenience retailer and an active payments issuer on the acceptance side. Its press room carried the launch of 'Petrol Pay Loyalty' (Sept 2025), described as the first non-bank Visa loyalty payment card in the region, plus EV-charging payment and instalment features via the Petrol GO app. Directly signals merchant-issued card and wallet strategy.
candidates.legal_status: public corporate communications; copyright of issuer
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Periodic crawl of the /sl/aktualno listing filtered by type=obvestilo-za-medije; capture title, date, body; mirror the parallel /en/ path for English releases
candidates.discovered_via_method: Slovenian-language search on retailer + payment terms, then snowball into corporate press room
queries_used: Petrol sporočila za javnost plačevanje kartice novica

candidates.source_name: Petrol d.d. – Petrol klub / plačilna kartica zvestobe product & terms pages
candidates.why_relevant: Product and general-terms pages (splošna pravila uporabe) reveal the issuing/processing arrangement, accepted schemes, instalment mechanics and the migration from the old Petrol klub card to Petrol Pay Loyalty. Terms PDFs are the most fact-dense merchant-side payments artefact.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Watch the /binaries/content/assets/ PDF paths for versioned 'splošna pravila' documents; diff versions to detect scheme/processor changes
candidates.discovered_via_method: Snowball from Petrol press release into product/terms tree
queries_used: Petrol sporočila za javnost plačevanje kartice novica

candidates.source_name: SPAR Slovenija – Mediji (press room) and customer-services payment pages
candidates.why_relevant: SPAR announced it was the first Slovenian retailer to accept Flik instant payments at POS terminals (via NLB Pay), a landmark acceptance-side event for A2A instant payments in Slovenia. Its media page and the dedicated FLIK service page are primary evidence of acceptance rollouts.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl /mediji listing on a weekly cadence; separately snapshot /informacije-za-kupce/storitve-za-kupce/flik for acceptance-scope changes
candidates.discovered_via_method: Slovenian-language retailer + wallet search, snowball into press room
queries_used: Mercator Spar Slovenija sporočilo za javnost novi način plačila mobilna denarnica

candidates.source_name: Mercator – Aktualno / Moj M mobile wallet and Pika payment card pages
candidates.why_relevant: Mercator operates the Pika card (a merchant-issued instalment payment card) and the Moj M / M Pay mobile wallet. Its news and general-terms pages document wallet launches, tokenised Pika-in-app payments and accepted payment types in the online store — the deepest merchant-issued credit footprint in Slovenian grocery.
candidates.source_subtype: corporate news + product terms + e-commerce FAQ
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monitor /aktualno news list plus the 'splošni pogoji' page for Moja Pika portal and Moj M app; also snapshot trgovina.mercator.si payment-methods FAQ for accepted-method changes
candidates.discovered_via_method: Slovenian-language search on wallet terms, snowball into product/terms pages
queries_used: Mercator Spar Slovenija sporočilo za javnost novi način plačila mobilna denarnica

candidates.source_name: Pošta Slovenije – Letna poročila (annual reports) and Denarne storitve
candidates.why_relevant: Pošta Slovenije is both a large corporate payments user and a retail payment-services outlet (money orders, bill payment, international money transfer). Its audited annual reports carry segment revenue for money services, and it is named in cash-access-network policy debates. State-controlled, so it also publishes 'informacije javnega značaja'.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Annual PDF harvest from the letna-porocila document folder; text-extract and keyword-scan for 'denarne storitve', 'plačilni promet'; also poll the 'objave po zakonu in kodeksu' page
candidates.discovered_via_method: Slovenian-language search on postal payment services + annual report terms
queries_used: Pošta Slovenije plačilne storitve novice letno poročilo PS Moneta

candidates.source_name: Telekom Slovenije – Javne objave (regulated disclosures) and Sporočila za medije
candidates.why_relevant: Listed issuer and a major biller/merchant: carrier billing, prepaid top-ups, mobile-payment partnerships and large recurring-collection volumes. Regulated disclosures plus a media room and a financial calendar make it a reliable, dated feed for corporate-user payment developments.
candidates.source_subtype: investor relations / regulated announcements + press room
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Poll /javne-objave and /sporocila-za-medije; cross-check against the same filings on SEOnet for dated, canonical versions; annual-report PDFs from /financna-porocila
candidates.discovered_via_method: Slovenian-language IR terminology search
queries_used: Telekom Slovenije sporočila za javnost odnosi z vlagatelji letno poročilo plačevanje

candidates.source_name: SEOnet – Ljubljana Stock Exchange regulated-announcement portal
candidates.why_relevant: Single canonical aggregator of dated regulated disclosures for all LJSE issuers, including merchant-side names in this cell (Petrol, Telekom Slovenije). Best snowball surface to enumerate which Slovenian corporate payment users are disclosure-obliged, and the authoritative timestamp for any release also posted on a corporate site.
candidates.access_status: public web; legacy ASPX query-string navigation, some doc_id deep links
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Enumerate issuers via doc=ISSUERS, then poll per-issuer announcement lists and PUBLIC_ANNOUNCMENTS; store doc_id as the stable key. Prefer polite crawl rates; no public API observed
candidates.discovered_via_method: Pointer-source reasoning (who must publish) then Slovenian-language search
queries_used: SEOnet Ljubljanska borza javne objave izdajatelji Petrol Telekom

candidates.source_name: Ljubljanski potniški promet (LPP) – Urbana city card and Urbana app news
candidates.why_relevant: Urbana is Slovenia's flagship closed-loop transit payment scheme; LPP publishes the migration to open-loop bank-card acceptance on buses, new validators, Bluetooth contactless validation and card top-up in the Urbana app. Ticketing acceptance is a leading indicator for contactless/open-loop rollout nationally.
candidates.source_subtype: transit operator news + scheme product pages
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Poll /aktualno plus the Urbana product pages; pair with Javni holding Ljubljana (jhl.si) media releases which carry the same announcements as PDFs
candidates.discovered_via_method: Slovenian-language transit/ticketing search, snowball into operator site
queries_used: Urbana LPP plačevanje s kartico nadgradnja javni prevoz Ljubljana brezstično

candidates.source_name: Javni holding Ljubljana (JHL) – sporočila za medije
candidates.why_relevant: Parent holding of LPP and other Ljubljana utilities; issues the formal PDF press releases behind Urbana app/payment announcements and other municipal-utility billing changes. Useful because the PDF releases are more detailed and more archivable than the operator news snippets.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl the aktualno/datoteke attachment paths for PDF releases; OCR not required, PDFs appear text-based
candidates.discovered_via_method: Snowball from LPP Urbana search result into parent holding press release PDF
queries_used: Urbana LPP plačevanje s kartico nadgradnja javni prevoz Ljubljana brezstično

candidates.source_name: Slovenske železnice – Potniški promet: ticketing, kartomati and payment terms
candidates.why_relevant: National rail operator documents accepted payment instruments on trains and at self-service ticket machines (cash, bank cards, and notably Flik), plus the general terms for kartomati. A concrete, dated record of A2A instant-payment acceptance spreading beyond retail into transport.
candidates.source_subtype: transport operator terms + ticketing pages (sl and en)
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Snapshot the 'splošni pogoji uporabe samopostrežnih prodajnih mest (kartomatov)' page and ticket-purchase pages; diff for changes in accepted instruments

candidates.source_name: IJPP – Integrirani javni potniški promet (national transport smartcard scheme)
candidates.why_relevant: Operator of the national IJPP chip card used across bus and rail. The scheme portal describes card issuance, subsidised-ticket flows and the data linkages behind them — the reference point for any move from closed-loop chip cards to open-loop bank-card acceptance in Slovenian public transport.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Low-frequency snapshot of scheme pages and any news/obvestila section; watch for tender or upgrade notices referencing EMV acceptance
candidates.discovered_via_method: Snowball from Slovenske železnice ticketing pages

candidates.source_name: Big Bang – e-commerce payment announcements and marketplace seller terms
candidates.why_relevant: Leading Slovenian consumer-electronics retailer and an early adopter on the acceptance side: online Flik payment, crypto acceptance via GoCrypto, and a marketplace whose seller terms name Mangopay as PSP. Merchant terms documents are one of the few public places where the acquirer/PSP relationship is actually disclosed.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Version-track the /upload/ terms PDFs (filenames are dated) and scan the akcije-popusti news path for payment-method launches

Its Slovenian newsroom/app pages are the primary record.

candidates.why_relevant: One of the largest Slovenian grocery chains by transaction count and a frequently quoted merchant on cash-versus-card mix. Its own communications cover self-checkout rollouts and digitalisation of sales systems, both of which drive acceptance-hardware and acquiring demand.

coverage_gaps.description: English-language coverage of this cell is thin: only one English query was run and it returned mostly non-Slovenian vendor and market-overview material rather than merchant primary sources.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run English queries against the /en/ mirrors of the merchant sites identified here (petrol.eu/en, spar.si English pages, telekom.si English IR) to capture the versions aimed at foreign investors, which often differ in detail.

coverage_gaps.description: Merchant-side acquirer and PSP relationships are almost never disclosed publicly; only Big Bang's marketplace seller terms (naming Mangopay) exposed one directly in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Systematically harvest merchant 'pogoji poslovanja' and checkout pages, and inspect public procurement notices (e-narocanje / JN portal) where state-owned merchants such as Pošta Slovenije, LPP and Slovenske železnice must tender for acquiring and POS services.

brief: The Slovenian acceptance side is unusually well documented at source: large merchants run their own press rooms and, in several cases, their own payment instruments — Petrol's Petrol Pay Loyalty Visa card, Mercator's Pika card and Moj M / M Pay wallet, Lidl's in-app payment — while SPAR and Big Bang publicly dated the arrival of Flik instant payments at POS and online respectively. Transport and municipal operators (LPP/Urbana, Slovenske železnice, IJPP, EasyPark and municipal news feeds) form a second, highly reliable layer that flags the shift from closed-loop cards toward open-loop and app-based acceptance. Listed names are anchored by SEOnet regulated disclosures, while the large non-listed grocers (Spar, Hofer, Lidl, Tuš) are reachable only through AJPES filings plus national-media quotes, which is where the coverage is thinnest. The main blind spots are utility and telco billers beyond Telekom, tolling, hospitality, and above all the acquirer/PSP relationships behind these merchants, which surface only in merchant terms documents and public procurement notices.
